descriptor: Sample data: an invented work order system used to show what a filled-in Command Center looks like.

requirements.statement: Sample: staff can create, update and close a work order.
Sample: a work order is never closed without a completion note.
Sample: assets are picked from the GIS map and fill in the work order.
Sample: residents can report an issue on a public page.
Sample: median time to close a pothole work order falls below 5 days.
Sample: the system connects to the GIS server and the public portal.

stories.title: Sample: create, update and close work orders
stories.narrative: As a field supervisor, I want to create and close work orders, so that crews know what to fix.

stories.title: Sample: pick assets from the GIS map
stories.narrative: As a dispatcher, I want to pick an asset on the map, so that its details fill in automatically.

stories.title: Sample: public issue reporting page
stories.narrative: As a resident, I want to report a broken streetlight, so that the city can fix it.

stories.title: Sample: connect GIS server and public portal
stories.narrative: As an administrator, I want the integrations to report their status, so that I know when one is down.

stories.title: Sample: measure time to close
stories.narrative: As a public works manager, I want to see time-to-close by type, so that I can tell whether we are improving.

agents.name: Sample: request triage agent
agents.purpose: Sample: reads new public requests and suggests a work type and priority for a dispatcher to confirm.
approval_gates: Dispatcher confirms before a work order is created
escalation_rules: Anything mentioning gas or injury goes straight to the on-call supervisor
